Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 19, verses 12–15:

{12} The preceding discourse indicated Yahya's birth, his youth and his upbringing. When he reached a stage at which he could understand speech, God commanded him to take the Book (al-kitab) with strength (bi-quwwah), that is, with earnestness and diligence. This is by striving to memorize its words, understand its meanings, and act upon its commands and prohibitions; this is the completion of taking the Book with strength. So he complied with his Lord's command, turned to the Book, memorized and understood it, and God placed in him an intelligence and perceptiveness not found in anyone else. Hence He said: ﴿And We gave him wisdom while still a child﴾ [i.e., knowledge of God's rulings and the ability to judge by them, while he was in his childhood and youth].

{13} And We also gave him ﴿compassion from Us﴾; that is, mercy and tenderness through which his affairs were made easy, his conditions were set right, and his actions were made upright. ﴿And purity﴾; that is, purity from defects and sins, so his heart became pure and his intellect became purified. This entails the removal of blameworthy attributes and bad character and the increase of good character and praiseworthy qualities. Hence He said: ﴿And he was righteous (taqiyyan)﴾; that is, one who performs what is commanded and abandons what is forbidden.

{14} Whoever is a believer and righteous becomes a friend of God, and is among the people of Paradise which is prepared for the righteous, and obtains of worldly and otherworldly reward what God has ordained for taqwa. He was also ﴿dutiful to his parents﴾; that is, he was not disobedient or harmful to his two parents, but was good to them in word and deed. ﴿And he was not arrogant or disobedient﴾; that is, he was not domineering or proud toward the worship of God, nor haughty toward the servants of God or toward his parents, but was humble, submissive, obedient and constantly turning back to God. Thus he combined fulfilling the right of God with fulfilling the rights of His creation.

{15} Hence he obtained safety from God in all his conditions, in their beginnings and their ends. Therefore He said: ﴿And peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive﴾. This implies his safety from Satan, from evil, and from punishment in these three states and what lies between them, and that he is safe from the Fire and the terrors, and is among the people of the Abode of Peace (dar al-salam). May the blessings and peace of God be upon him, upon his father, and upon all the messengers, and may He make us among their followers; indeed He is Generous and Bountiful.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 19, verses 22–26:

{22} That is, when she conceived Jesus, peace be upon him, she feared scandal, so she withdrew from the people to a remote place.

{23} When her delivery drew near, the pains of labor drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. When the pain of childbirth afflicted her, along with the distress of being alone, without food or drink, and the pain in her heart from what people would say, and she feared she would not be patient, she wished that she had died before this event and had become "forgotten, out of mind" (nasyan mansiyyan), so that she would not be mentioned. This wish arose from that distressing condition, and there was no good or benefit for her in this wish; rather, good and benefit lie in what Allah has decreed to occur.

{24} Then the angel calmed her fear and steadied her heart, and called to her from beneath her, perhaps from a place lower than where she was, and said to her: "Do not grieve," that is, do not be distressed or worried; "your Lord has provided beneath you a stream (sariyy)," that is, a river from which you may drink.

{25} "And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates (ruṭaban janiyyan)," that is, fresh, delicious and beneficial.

{26} "So eat," of the dates, "and drink," from the river, "and be comforted in your eye," by Jesus. This was her reassurance regarding being spared the pain of childbirth and receiving wholesome food and drink. As for the matter of what people would say, she was commanded that when she saw any human being, she should indicate by gesture: "Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast (sawm)," that is, silence, "so I will not speak today to any human being (insiyyan)," that is, do not address them with speech, so that you may be relieved of their talk and their words. She was not commanded to speak to them to clear herself of the accusation, because the people would not believe her and it would be of no benefit. Therefore the proof of this extraordinary event was made something of its own kind: the speech of Jesus while still very young. For this reason, the Most High said:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 19, verses 34–36:

{34–35} That is, the one described with these attributes is Jesus, son of Mary, without any doubt or dispute, rather {the word of truth} and the speech of God, than which none is more truthful in saying nor better in narration. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 19, verses 39–40:

{39–40} Al-Inḏar (warning) is informing about that which is feared, in a manner that instills dread, and describing its attributes. The most deserving of what people are warned about and made to fear is the Day of Regret (yawm al-ḥasrah), when the matter is decided, and the first and the last are gathered in a single place, and they are questioned about their deeds. Whoever believes in Allah and follows His messengers will be granted a happiness after which there is no misery; and whoever does not believe in Allah and does not follow His messengers will be granted a misery after which there is no happiness, and will have lost himself and his family. Then he will regret and feel remorse, a remorse by which hearts are cut off and hearts are shattered. And what regret is greater than the loss of Allah's pleasure and His Garden, and the deserving of His wrath and the Fire, in a state where he cannot return to resume work, and has no way to change his condition by going back to the world?! This is before them, while they are in the world, heedless of this great matter; it does not occur to their hearts, and if it does occur, it is only in passing heedlessness. Heedlessness has overwhelmed them, and drunkenness has enveloped them. They do not believe in Allah and do not follow His messengers; their desires have distracted them, and their transient, perishing lusts have come between them and faith. The world and all that is in it, from its beginning to its end, will depart from its people and they will depart from it, and Allah will inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and He will return them to Himself and recompense them for what they did therein, and for what they lost or gained therein. So whoever does good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame none but himself.

The most excellent, most virtuous and most exalted of books is this Clear Book and Wise Reminder (al-Kitab al-Mubin wa'l-Dhikr al-Hakim). If it mentions reports, it is the truest, most deserving and most beneficial of reports; if it mentions commands and prohibitions, they are the most sublime and most just and equitable commands and prohibitions; if it mentions recompense, promise and threat, it is the truest and most deserving of reports and the most indicative of wisdom, justice and bounty. And if it mentions the prophets and messengers, then what is mentioned of them is more complete and more excellent than other things. For this reason, it often repeats and expands upon the stories of the prophets whom Allah preferred over others, and raised in rank and exalted their station, because of what they undertook of worshipping Allah, loving Him, turning to Him in repentance, fulfilling His rights and the rights of His servants, calling creation to Allah, patience in that, and their splendid stations and lofty abodes. So Allah mentioned in this surah a collection of the prophets, and commanded His Messenger to mention them, for in mentioning them is the manifestation of praise to Allah and to them, and the clarification of His favour and beneficence toward them, and in it is the exhortation to believe in them, love them and follow their example. Thus He said:

This is a clear proof that worshipping what is deficient in its essence and actions is abominable by reason and by law. His admonition and allusion indicate that what is obligatory and fitting to worship is the One who possesses perfection, from whom alone the servants receive any blessing, and who alone repels any calamity from them, and He is God, exalted.

{43} {O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you}; that is: O my father, do not belittle me and say, "I am your son, and you have what I do not have." Rather, God has given me knowledge that He has not given you. The purpose of this is his saying: {so follow me, I will guide you to a path, balanced}; that is, upright and moderate, which is the worship of God alone without partner, and obedience to Him in all circumstances.
In this there is a gentleness and softness of address that is not hidden, for he did not say, "O my father, I am knowledgeable and you are ignorant," or, "You have no knowledge at all." The Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, progressed in calling his father from the easiest to the easiest: he informed him of his knowledge, that this necessitates his following me, and that if you obey me, you will be guided to a straight path. Then he forbade him from worshipping Satan and informed him of the harms in it. Then he warned him of God's punishment and retribution if he persisted in his state, and that he would be a protector of Satan.

{46} This supplication did not benefit that wretched man, and he answered with the answer of an ignorant one and said: {Are you turning away from my gods, O Abraham?}: he boasted of his gods, which are of stone and idols, and blamed Abraham for his aversion to them. This is from extreme ignorance and grievous disbelief: he praises the worship of idols and calls to them. {If you do not desist}; that is, from reviling my gods and calling to the worship of God, {I will surely stone you}; that is, kill you by stoning, {and leave me alone a long time}; that is, do not speak to me for a long period.

{47} The Friend answered him with the answer of the servants of the Most Merciful when addressed by the ignorant. He did not revile him, but was patient, and did not repay his father with what he disliked, and said: {Peace be upon you}; that is, you will be safe from my addressing you with insult, abuse, and what you dislike. {I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord; indeed, He has been ever Gracious to me}; that is, I will not cease calling upon God for you, for guidance and forgiveness, that He guide you to Islam, by which forgiveness is attained; for He has been ever Gracious to me, that is, merciful and kind toward my condition, attentive to me. He continued to seek God's forgiveness for him, hoping that God would guide him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, and that nothing would benefit him, he ceased seeking forgiveness for him and disassociated himself from him.
God has commanded us to follow the religion of Abraham. From following his creed is to take his path in calling to God with knowledge, wisdom, gentleness and ease, moving from one level to another, patience in that, not being weary of it, patience over the harm the caller receives from people by word and deed, and responding to that with pardon and forgiveness, and indeed with good treatment in word and deed.

{48} When he despaired of his people and his father, he said: {I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides God}; that is, you and your idols, {and I will call upon my Lord}: this includes both the supplication of worship and the supplication of request, {perhaps I will not be in my supplication to my Lord unfortunate}; that is, perhaps God will make me happy by answering my supplication and accepting my deeds. This is the duty of one who has despaired of those he called, who followed their desires, for admonitions did not benefit them, and they persisted in their transgression, wandering blindly: that he occupy himself with reforming himself, hope for acceptance from his Lord, and withdraw from evil and its people.

{57} {And We raised him to a high station}; that is: Allah raised his mention among the worlds and his rank among those brought near, so he was high in mention and high in station.

{58} When He mentioned these noble prophets and chosen messengers, and mentioned their virtues and ranks, He said: {Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets}; that is, Allah bestowed upon them a blessing that cannot be matched and a grace that cannot be preceded, namely prophethood and messengerhood. They are the ones whose path we were commanded to ask Allah to guide us to, saying: ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor﴾, and that whoever obeys Allah will be ﴿with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets...﴾ [4:69], the verse; and that some of them are ﴿from the offspring of Adam and of those We carried with Noah﴾; that is, from his offspring. ﴿And from the offspring of Abraham and Israel﴾. These are the best houses in the world, whom Allah chose, selected, and elevated. Their state, when the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, containing information about the unseen, the attributes of the All-Knowing of the unseen, and information about the Last Day, promise and threat, was: ﴿they fell down prostrating and weeping﴾; that is, they humbled themselves before the verses of Allah and were humbled by them, and what the verses impressed upon their hearts of faith, desire, and fear caused them to weep, turn in repentance, and prostrate to their Lord. They were not among those who, when the verses of Allah were recited to them, fell down upon them deaf and blind.

In attributing the verses to His name "the Most Merciful" there is an indication that His verses are among His mercy toward His servants and His kindness to them, since through them He guided them to the truth, gave them sight after blindness, rescued them from misguidance, and taught them what they did not know.

{59} When the Exalted mentioned these prophets, who were sincere, who followed the pleasure of their Lord and turned penitently to Him, He then mentioned those who came after them and altered what they had been commanded. {Then there came after them a generation} (khalf): they went back to the rear and to what lies behind. {And they neglected the prayer} (al-salat), which they had been commanded to guard and establish. They were lax about it and wasted it. When they neglected the prayer, which is the pillar of the religion, the measure of faith and sincerity toward the Lord of the worlds, the most emphatic of deeds and the best of qualities, they were even more neglectful of everything else in their religion and more ready to abandon it. The impelling cause of this is that they followed the desires of their own souls and their wills, so their aims became directed toward them, placing them ahead of the rights of God. From this arose their neglect of His rights and their pursuit of their souls' desires whenever these appeared to them, which they obtained by any means that came to hand. {So they will encounter error} (ghayy): that is, severe, multiplied punishment.

{60} Then the Exalted made an exception, saying: {Except for those who repent} from polytheism, innovations and sins, abandoning them, regretting them, and resolving firmly never to return to them; {and believe} in God, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day; {and do righteous deeds}, meaning the deeds that God prescribed through His messengers when performed seeking His countenance. {Those} who combine repentance, faith and righteous deeds {will enter Paradise}, which contains everlasting bliss, a sound life, and the nearness of the Generous Lord, {and they will not be wronged in anything}: in their deeds. Rather, they will find them complete, their rewards fully given and multiplied in number.

{61} Then He mentioned that the Paradise He promised them is not like other gardens, but rather {Gardens of Eden} (jannat 'adn): that is, gardens of permanent residence, with no departure from them, no removal and no cessation. This is due to their vastness and the abundance of good, joy, delight and happiness within them. {Which the Most Merciful promised His servants in the unseen}: that is, which the Most Merciful promised. He attributed them to His name the Most Merciful because they contain mercy and kindness such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. He named them His mercy, saying: {As for those whose faces will be whitened, they will be in the mercy of God, abiding therein forever} (Qur'an 3:107). Also, attributing them to His mercy indicates the continuity of their joy and that they endure as long as His mercy endures, which is their effect and requirement.

The servants (ʿibad) meant in this verse are the servants of His divinity, who worshipped Him and adhered to His laws, so servitude became a description of them, as in His saying: {And the servants of the Most Merciful} (25:63) and similar. This is distinct from His servants in the sense of mere subjects who did not worship Him. Those, although they are servants of His lordship, since He created, provided for and governed them, are not included among the servants of His divinity, the voluntary servitude for which its bearer is praised. Their servitude is compelled, with no praise for them in it.

As for His saying {in the unseen}, it may be connected to "promised by the Most Merciful." The meaning then is that God promised them this promise, unseen, which they had not witnessed or beheld; yet they believed in it, affirmed its unseen reality, and strove for it as it deserves, although they had not seen it. How much more so if they had seen it: they would have been even more eager for it, greater in desire for it, and more zealous for it. In this there is praise for them for their belief in the unseen, which is beneficial faith.

It may also be connected to "His servants," meaning those who worshipped Him in their state of absence and not seeing Him. This is their worship though they have not seen Him; if they had seen Him, they would have been even more devoted in worship, greater in turning to Him, more loving, and more longing.

It may also be that the meaning is: these gardens which the Most Merciful promised His servants are among matters that descriptions cannot grasp and that no one knows except God. In this there is an arousing of longing for them and a general description that stirs souls and disturbs those at rest from seeking them. This is like His saying: {No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do} (32:17).

All these meanings are sound and established, but the first possibility is preferable, by the evidence of His saying: {Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled} (19:61): it must come to pass, for He does not break His promise, and He is the most truthful of speakers.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 19, verses 64–65:

{64} The Prophet (ﷺ) once delayed in asking Jibril (peace be upon him) to descend to him, so he said to him: "If only you would visit us more often than you do," out of longing for him and a sense of loneliness at being parted from him, and so that his heart would be reassured by his descent. Then Allah, the Exalted, sent down upon the tongue of Jibril: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾. That is: we have no say in the matter; if He commands us, we hasten to carry out His command and do not disobey Him in anything, just as He said of them: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾. So we are servants who are commanded. ﴿To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that﴾. That is: to Him belong the past, future, and present matters, in time and in place. When it becomes clear that the whole matter belongs to Allah, and that we are servants who are managed, the question remains whether the divine wisdom requires it, so He carries it out, or does not require it, so He postpones it. Hence He said: ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾. That is: Allah would not forget you and neglect you, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your Lord has not bid you farewell, nor has He abandoned you﴾. Rather, He has always been attentive to your affairs, dealing with you in His finest customs and His beautiful arrangements. That is: if our descent is delayed beyond the usual time, then do not let that grieve you or concern you, and know that Allah is the One who willed that, because of the wisdom He has in it.

{65} Then He gave the reason for the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and His not forgetting, namely that He is ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾. His lordship over the heavens and the earth, and their existence in the most excellent and perfect order, in which there is no heedlessness, no neglect, no purposelessness, and no vanity, is a decisive proof of His all-encompassing knowledge. So do not occupy yourself with that; rather occupy yourself with what benefits you and whose fruit returns to you, which is worshipping Him alone, with no partner. ﴿And be steadfast in His worship﴾. That is: restrain yourself upon it, strive against yourself, and stand in it in the most complete and perfect manner according to your ability. In occupying oneself with the worship of Allah there is consolation for the worshipper from all attachments and desires, just as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not stretch your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them, the splendor of the life of this world, that We may test them therein...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it...﴾, the verse. ﴿Do you know of any who is named like Him?﴾. That is: do you know of anyone among the creatures who shares His name, resembles Him, or is equal to Him? This is an interrogative with the meaning of negation, known by reason; that is: you know of no one who shares His name or resembles Him. For He is the Lord and others are the lorded-over; He is the Creator and others are created; He is the Self-Sufficient in every respect, and others are poor in essence in every respect; He is the Perfect, to whom belongs absolute perfection in every respect, and others are deficient, possessing no perfection except what Allah, the Exalted, has given them. This is a decisive proof that Allah alone deserves to be singled out for worship, that His worship is the truth, and that the worship of anything else is false. Therefore He commanded worship of Him alone and steadfastness in it, and He gave the reason for that as His perfection and His singularity in greatness and the Most Beautiful Names.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 19, verses 68–70:

{68} God, who is the most truthful of those who speak of His lordship, swears an oath that He will surely gather these deniers of the Resurrection, together with their devils, and then bring them together at the appointed time of a known day. {Then We will surely bring them forth around Hell on their knees}; that is, kneeling from the severity of the terrors, the abundance of the tremors, and the dreadfulness of the circumstances, awaiting the judgment of the Great, the Exalted.

{69} For this reason He mentions His judgment concerning them, saying: {Then We will surely single out from every faction whichever of them is most insolent towards the Most Merciful}; that is, We will single out from every group and party of the wrongdoers who share in injustice, disbelief and insolence the one who is most insolent, the greatest in wrongdoing and the greatest in disbelief, and We will bring him forward to the punishment. Then, in the same way, We will bring forward to the punishment the one who is next most grave in sin, and so on. In that state they curse one another, each cursing the other, and the last of them will say to the first of them: {Our Lord, these have led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire} [He said: for each there is double, but you do not know], and the first of them will say to the last of them: {You had no superiority over us...}

{70} All of this follows from His justice, His wisdom and His vast knowledge. For this reason He says: {Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein}; that is, Our knowledge encompasses whoever is most deserving of burning in the Fire. We know them, and We know their deeds, what they merit, and their proportionate share of punishment.

{73} That is: when Our clear verses are recited to these disbelievers, verses clearly indicating the oneness of God and the truthfulness of His messengers, which ought to produce true faith and firm certainty in whoever hears them, they respond to them with the opposite of what is due to them. They mock them and those who believe in them, and they take their good worldly condition as proof that they are better than the believers. Opposing the truth, they say: {Which of the two groups}; that is, we or the believers, {is better in station}; that is, in this world, through abundance of wealth and children and superiority in pleasures. {And better in assembly}; that is, in gathering. So they draw a conclusion from this corrupt premise, because they have more wealth and children, and most of their worldly aims have been achieved, and their gatherings and councils are adorned and ornamented, while the believers are the opposite of this condition. Therefore, they are better than the believers!!

{74} This is an argument of utmost corruption, and it is a case of reversing realities. Otherwise, abundance of wealth and children and fine appearance are often a cause of the ruin, misery and evil of their possessor. For this reason, the Exalted said: {And how many generations have We destroyed before them, who were better in furnishing}; that is, in goods, such as utensils, furnishings, houses and ornaments, {and in appearance}; that is, better in look and appearance, in the bounty of living, the joy of pleasures and beauty of forms. If those destroyed ones were better than them in furnishings and appearance, and that did not prevent the punishment from descending upon them, then how can these, who are fewer and weaker than them, be safe from punishment? {Are your disbelievers better than those, or do you have immunity in the scriptures?}?! It is known from this that deducing the excellence of the Hereafter from the excellence of this world is one of the most corrupt of proofs, and it is one of the methods of the disbelievers.

**{75}** When he had mentioned their false argument, which indicates the intensity of their obstinacy and the strength of their misguidance, he here informed that whoever is in error, by being content with it for himself and striving in it, Allah extends him in it and increases his love for it, as a punishment for his choosing it over guidance. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾, and ﴿We turn their hearts and their sight away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾.

﴿Until when they see﴾; i.e., the speakers (of the statement) ﴿which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly﴾, ﴿what they are promised, either the punishment﴾: by killing or otherwise, ﴿or the Hour﴾: which is the gate of recompense for deeds. ﴿Then they will know who is worse in position and weaker in forces﴾; i.e., then it will become clear to them that their claim is false, and that it is a claim that will collapse, and they will be certain that they are the people of evil and weaker in forces. But this knowledge will not benefit them at all, because it will not be possible for them to return to the world so that they may act other than their former deeds.

{76} When He mentioned that He extends (the term of) the wrongdoers in their misguidance, He mentioned that He increases the guided in guidance, out of His grace and mercy towards them. Guidance (al-huda) encompasses beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds. Thus, whoever treads a path in knowledge, faith and righteous deeds, Allah increases him in it, facilitates it for him, makes it easy for him, and bestows upon him other matters that do not fall within his own acquisition. In this is evidence for the increase and decrease of faith, as stated by the pious predecessors (al-salaf al-salih).

Its evidence is also the Almighty's saying: ﴿That those who believe may increase in faith﴾ and ﴿When His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith﴾. Its evidence also is the reality, for faith is the saying of the heart and tongue, and the action of the heart, tongue and limbs, and believers differ greatly in these matters.

Then He said: ﴿And the enduring righteous deeds﴾; that is, the lasting deeds that do not cease when others cease, and do not perish. These are the righteous ones among them: prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, 'umrah, recitation, glorification (tasbih), magnifying God (takbir), praising God (tahmid), declaring God's oneness (tahlil), kindness to created beings, and deeds of the heart and body. ﴿These are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for return﴾; that is, their reward and recompense are better with Allah, and their benefit and return are abundant for those who perform them. This is the use of the comparative form (af'al al-tafdil) outside its usual sense, for there is no other deed that benefits and whose reward remains for its doer and is fruitful, other than the enduring righteous deeds. Its connection is the mention of the enduring righteous deeds. And Allah knows best: when He mentioned that the wrongdoers regarded the conditions of this world, such as wealth, children, fine standing, and the like, as a sign of the good state of their possessor, He here informed that the matter is not as they claimed; rather, the deed that is the mark of happiness and the banner of success is acting in accordance with what Allah loves and is pleased with.

{77} That is: Do you not marvel at the state of this disbeliever, who combines his disbelief in the signs of Allah with his grand claim that he will be given wealth and children in the Hereafter, meaning that he will be among the people of Paradise? This is among the most astonishing things. Had he been a believer in Allah and made this claim, the matter would have been easier.
Although this verse was revealed concerning a specific disbeliever, it encompasses every disbeliever who claims that he is upon the truth and that he is among the people of Paradise.

{78} Allah said, rebuking and refuting him: ﴿Has he attained knowledge of the unseen?﴾; that is, has his knowledge encompassed the unseen so that he knows what will happen, and that among what will happen is that he will be given wealth and children on the Day of Resurrection? ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾: that he will attain what he has said; that is, none of that has happened, so it is known that he is a fabricator, speaking of what he has no knowledge of. This division and questioning is of the utmost force in argument and establishing proof, for the one who claims that he will have a good portion with Allah in the Hereafter is in one of two situations: either his statement issues from knowledge of future unseen matters, and it is known that this belongs to Allah alone, so no one knows any future unseen matters except what Allah has disclosed to him of His messengers; or he has taken a covenant with Allah through belief in Him and following His messengers, whom Allah has promised for their people, and whom He has declared to be the people of the Hereafter, the saved and the successful. When these two matters are negated, the falsehood of the claim is known thereby.

{83} This is among the punishments of the disbelievers: because they did not take refuge in God, nor hold fast to the rope of God, but instead associated others with Him and allied themselves with His enemies, the devils, He gave them dominion over them and assigned them to them. So the devils began to incite them toward sins with fierce incitement, and to drive them toward disbelief with forceful driving. They whisper to them, they inspire them, they adorn falsehood for them, and they make truth repugnant to them. Thus the love of falsehood enters their hearts and soaks into them, and they strive for it as one who is right strives for his right, supporting it with all their effort, fighting on its behalf, and waging jihad for falsehood against the people of truth. All of this is their recompense for their allegiance to their own protector and their alliance with His enemy: He gave Satan authority over them. Otherwise, if they had believed in God and relied upon Him, Satan would have had no authority over them, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾.

{84} ﴿So do not be hasty against them﴾; that is, against these disbelievers who seek to hasten the punishment. ﴿We are only counting out for them a count﴾; that is, they have appointed days that are numbered; they will neither go ahead of them nor fall behind them. We give them respite and forbear with them for a period so that they may reconsider the command of God. If that does not benefit them, We seize them with the seizure of One Mighty and Omnipotent.

{85} He, may He be exalted, informs of the difference between the two groups: the God-fearing (al-muttaqin) and the criminals (al-mujrimin). The God-fearing, by guarding themselves against shirk (associating partners with God), innovation (bid'ah) and sins, will be gathered to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection honored, esteemed and magnified. Their destination is the All-Merciful (al-Rahman), and their aim is the Bountiful Giver (al-Mannan), as a delegation (wafdan) to Him. The one who comes as a delegation must have in his heart the hope and good opinion of the One he comes to, to a known degree. So the God-fearing come to the All-Merciful hoping for His mercy, His abundant kindness, and success in obtaining His gifts in the abode of His good pleasure. This is because of what they put forward of works done in His piety and following what pleases Him, and because God promised them this reward through the tongues of His messengers. So they turn toward their Lord, reassured by it and confident in His bounty.

{86} As for the criminals, they will be driven {to Hell as a thirsty herd} (wirdan); that is, parched with thirst. This is the most wretched of states: they are driven in a manner of humiliation and degradation to the greatest prison and the most dreadful punishment, which is Hell, in a state of thirst and exhaustion. They cry for help but are not helped, they call out but are not answered, and they seek intercession but no intercession is granted to them.

{87} For this reason He said: {they will have no power of intercession}; that is, intercession is not theirs to possess, nor do they have any share in it, for it belongs to God, the Exalted: {Say: to God belongs all intercession}. He has informed that the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them, because they did not take a covenant with Him by believing in Him and His messengers. Otherwise, whoever takes a covenant with Him, believes in Him and His messengers, and follows them, is among those whom God has approved, and intercession is attained for him, as God, the Exalted, said: {and they intercede only for him whom He approves}. God called belief in Him and following His messengers a "covenant" (ahd) because it is a covenant stated in His books and on the tongues of His messengers, with a beautiful reward for those who follow them.

{96} This is among His blessings upon His servants who combine faith and righteous deeds: that He promises them that He will place for them affection (wudd), i.e., love and warmth in the hearts of His allies (awliya') and the people of the heavens and the earth. When they have affection in hearts, many of their affairs are made easy for them, and they obtain goodness, supplications in their favor, guidance, acceptance, and leadership to the extent that they do. This is why it is related in the authentic hadith: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril: 'Indeed I love so-and-so, so love him.' So Jibril loves him, then he calls out among the people of the heavens: 'Indeed Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.' So the people of the heavens love him, then acceptance is placed for him on the earth." And Allah placed affection for them only because they loved Him and loved Him in return; so He caused them to be loved by His allies and His beloved ones.

{97} He, the Exalted, informs of His blessing: that He made this noble Qur'an easy by means of the tongue of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). He made its words and meanings easy so that its purpose and benefit might be achieved. ﴿So that you may give glad tidings thereby to the righteous (al-muttaqin)﴾, by encouraging them toward what is promised of reward, both swift and deferred, and by mentioning the causes that necessitate the glad tidings, ﴿and warn thereby a people (qawman) contentious (ludd)﴾; that is, fierce in their falsehood and strong in their disbelief. So you warn them, the proof is established against them, the clear path is made evident to them, and whoever perishes, perishes after clear evidence, and whoever lives, lives after clear evidence.

{98} Then He threatened them with the destruction of those who denied before them, saying: ﴿And how many generations (qarn) have We destroyed before them?﴾ From the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh and others of the obstinate deniers, when they persisted in their transgression, Allah destroyed them, so none of them remains. ﴿Do you perceive from them anyone, or hear from them a faint sound (rikz)?﴾ Al-rikz is a hidden sound; that is, no trace or vestige of them remains. Rather, their reports remain as a lesson for those who take heed, and their tales a warning for those who are admonished.

The tafsir of Surah Maryam is complete. And to Allah belong all praise and thanks.
